record.title: The multi-away multiline-queue enumeration conjecture
record.statement:
Let $N\ge n$, let $\mathbf{k}=(k_1\ge\cdots\ge k_r\ge 1)$ be a partition, and let $\mathbf{k}'$ be its conjugate. For $S\subseteq [r]$, let $\mathbf{k}(S)$ be the partition consisting of the parts $k_i$ with $i\in S$, and let $\mathbf{k}(S)'$ be its conjugate. Define $A_S$ to have entries

$$
\binom{b_i+j-1-k_{n+1-i}(S)'}{j-1-k_{n+1-i}(S)'}.
$$

Here $k_i(S)'=0$ if $i>k_{\min S}$. Assume $n>k_1>k_2+1>k_3+2>\dots>k_r+r-1>r-1$ and $0\le b_1<\dots<b_n\le N-1$. **The multi-away MLQ enumeration conjecture.** The number of multiline queues is

$$
G_{s_{k_1}\dots s_{k_r}w_0}(b_1,\dots,b_n;N)=\sum_{S\subseteq [r]}(-1)^{|S|}\prod_{i\in S}\binom{N}{k_i}\det A_S.
$$

This generalizes the one-away formula to commuting simple reflections. The case $r=1$ specializes to the one-away conjecture, and the paper does not provide a proof of the general statement.
record.source_name: Erik Aas and Svante Linusson, “Continuous Multi-line Queues and TASEP”, arXiv:1501.04417 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.04417

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: The planar signed projective-cube homomorphism conjecture
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 2$. A **signed graph** is a graph together with a distinguished set of negative edges; its **unbalanced-girth** is the length of its shortest cycle containing an odd number of negative edges. A signed graph is **consistent** when its sign structure satisfies the consistency condition used in the source. Let $\mathcal{SPC}_d$ denote the signed projective cube obtained from the Cayley graph

$$
\mathcal{PC}_d=(\mathbb{Z}_2^d,\{e_1,e_2,\cdots,e_d,J\})
$$

by assigning positive signs to edges corresponding to $e_i$ and negative signs to edges corresponding to $J$. A signed-graph homomorphism preserves adjacency and signs up to switching. **The planar signed projective-cube homomorphism conjecture.** Every planar consistent signed graph of unbalanced-girth $d+1$ admits a homomorphism to $\mathcal{SPC}_d$. The paper identifies this as the focus of the work and attributes it to earlier sources; the supplied status evidence says the question was answered in a larger framework, so this conjecture is treated as solved.
record.source_name: Reza Naserasr, Sagnik Sen and Qiang Sun, “Walk-powers and homomorphism bound of planar graphs”, arXiv:1501.05089 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.05089

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: The constant-boundary enumeration conjecture for tree $sl_n$ webs
record.statement:
Let $R_{p,r}(k)$ denote the generalized Catalan number associated with parameters $p,r,k$. An $sl_n$ web is a diagrammatic object for the representation theory of $U_q(sl_n)$; a web **lacks an internal cycle** when its underlying graph has no cycle away from the boundary, and its boundary string records the labels on its boundary edges. **Constant-boundary enumeration conjecture.** For any $n \geq 3$, $ (n-2)^k R_{n+1,n-1}(k)$ equals the number of connected $sl_n$ webs that lack an internal cycle and have a boundary string with $n(k+1)$ total 1's.
This conjecture generalizes the preceding enumeration result for $A_2$ (or $sl_3$) webs to tree webs for $sl_n$. It remains open because the coral-diagram interpretation requires proving the number of valid, non-equivalent choices for the base and each $(n+1)$-star, as well as showing that distinct pieces do not interact to produce further relations.
record.source_name: Jonathan E. Beagley and Paul Drube, “Generalized Catalan Numbers and the Enumeration of Planar Embeddings”, arXiv:1501.07137 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1501.07137

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2015).

record.title: The cycle-membership conjecture for exact skew-symmetric plane permutations
record.statement:
Let $[n]^*$ and $[n]^{-}$ denote the signed sets used for the plane permutation, let $p_r$ be the reversal permutation, and let $D_{\mathfrak{p}}$ denote the diagonal permutation of the plane permutation $\mathfrak{p}=(\tilde{s},\pi)$. Assume that $\mathfrak{p}$ is exact and skew-symmetric on $[n]^*\cup[n]^{-}$, that $D_{\mathfrak{p}}=p_r^{-1}$, and that

$$
\pi(s_{i-1})=s_{2n+1-i}
$$

for some $1\leq i\leq n$.

**Cycle-membership conjecture.** The elements $n$ and $s_n$ belong to the same cycle of $\pi$.

This conjecture addresses the critical case in the analysis of 2-reversals for signed permutations, where the standard lemma does not apply. Establishing the asserted cycle membership would allow the use of the alternative transpose lemma to obtain a 2-reversal in this remaining case; the supplied text gives examples but no proof or resolution.
record.source_name: Ricky X. F. Chen and Christian M. Reidys, “Plane permutations and applications to a result of Zagier-Stanley and distances of permutations”, arXiv:1502.07674 (2016).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1502.07674

record.title: Conjecture on bounded doubling of large-spectrum sets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be the ambient finite abelian group, and for a subset $A$ of $G$ let $\text{Spec}_{\varepsilon}(A)$ denote its $\varepsilon$-spectrum. Fix $0<\delta<\alpha<1/2$ and $0<\varepsilon<1/2$. Let $A\subseteq G$ satisfy $|A|\geq |G|^\alpha$.

**Bounded-doubling spectrum conjecture.** There exists a subset $A'\subseteq A$ with $|A'|\geq |A|/C$ such that

$$
|\text{Spec}_{\varepsilon}(A')+\text{Spec}_{\varepsilon}(A')|\leq C|G|^\delta\cdot|\text{Spec}_{\varepsilon}(A')|,
$$

where $C=C(\varepsilon,\delta)$.

This conjecture asserts that, after passing to a large subset, the $\varepsilon$-spectrum has bounded doubling up to the factor $|G|^\delta$. The preceding theorem establishes a related result after changing the spectrum threshold from $\varepsilon$ to a smaller value, while the conjecture asks for the conclusion at the original threshold.
record.source_name: Kaave Hosseini and Shachar Lovett, “On the structure of the spectrum of small sets”, arXiv:1504.01059 (2015).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1504.01059

record.title: The 4-cycle obstruction conjecture for κ-matroidal connectivity functions
record.statement:
Let $E$ be a finite set, and let $
u$ be the connectivity function on $\\{a,b,c,d\\}$ defined by

$$
\nu(\{a\})=\nu(\{b\})=\nu(\{c\})=\nu(\{d\})=1,
$$

$$
\nu(\{a,b\})=\nu(\{b,c\})=1,\qquad \nu(\{a,c\})=2,
$$

and with all other values determined by symmetry. A connectivity function is **unitary** when its singleton values are at most one, and it is **κ-matroidal** when it is obtained by the operation $\mu\downarrow (E-D)$ from a matroidal connectivity function. **The 4-cycle obstruction conjecture.** Let $\mu$ be a unitary connectivity function on $E$. Then $\mu$ is κ-matroidal if and only if there is no subset $D\subseteq E$ such that $\mu\downarrow (E-D)$ is isomorphic to $\nu$. The conjecture proposes that the connectivity function arising from a 4-cycle is the only obstruction to being κ-matroidal, a property that is minor-closed under the operation defined in the source. Its status is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Susan Jowett, Songbao Mo and Geoff Whittle, “Connectivity Functions and Polymatroids”, arXiv:1605.01455 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1605.01455

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2016).

record.title: The period characterization conjecture for three-element subtraction games
record.statement:
Let $S(s_1,s_2,s_3)$ be a subtraction game with $s_1<s_2<s_3$, and suppose its nim sequence $n_0n_1n_2n_3n_4\ldots$ is eventually periodic with period $p$. In Case I, assume $s_3=s_1+s_2$ and define $j$ by

$$
0\leq j<2s_1,\qquad s_2-s_1\equiv j\pmod{2s_1}.
$$

In Case II, assume $s_3\ne s_1+s_2$.

**Period characterization conjecture.** In Case I,

$$
p=\begin{cases}
s_2+s_3-j&\text{if }0\leq j<s_1,\\
\dfrac{s_1(s_2+s_3+j-2s_1)}{\operatorname{gcd}(s_1,2s_1-j)}&\text{if }s_1\leq j<2s_1.
\end{cases}
$$

In Case II, $p$ has one of seven potential values: it is a divisor of at least one of the numbers $s_i+s_j$ for $1\leq i<j\leq3$, and is exactly the greatest common divisor of all such terms. Equivalently,

$$
p=\operatorname{gcd}_{(i,j)\in\mathcal{G}}(s_i+s_j),
$$

where $\mathcal{G}$ is the set of pairs $(i,j)$ such that $s_i+s_j$ is a multiple of $p$.

The conjecture seeks a complete characterization of the eventual periods of nim sequences for subtraction games whose subtraction set has size three. The paper presents this as a general formula extending known results for particular families and notes that the periods remain largely mysterious; no resolution is supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Mark Daniel Ward, “A Conjecture about Periods in Subtraction Games”, arXiv:1606.04029 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.04029

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2016).

record.title: Reiner–Tenner–Yong's first shifted Young lattice CDE conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\delta_r=(r,r-1,\ldots,1)$, and for partitions let $\nu+\lambda$ denote the partition obtained by adding corresponding parts. For $a,m,n\geq 1$ with $n>am$, set

$$
\lambda:=\delta_n+\delta_m\circ a^a.
$$

Here $[\varnothing,\lambda]_{\mathrm{shift}}$ is the initial interval of the shifted Young's lattice, $\mathrm{uni}_{[\varnothing,\lambda]_{\mathrm{shift}}}$ is its uniform distribution, and $\mathrm{ddeg}$ denotes down-degree. **Reiner–Tenner–Yong's first shifted Young lattice conjecture.** The interval $[\varnothing,\lambda]_{\mathrm{shift}}$ is CDE, with edge density

$$
\mathbb{E}(\mathrm{uni}_{[\varnothing,\lambda]_{\mathrm{shift}}};\mathrm{ddeg})=\frac{n+1+am}{4}.
$$

This is one of two conjectures concerning CDE initial intervals of the shifted Young's lattice; the source proves this conjecture, so it is no longer open.
record.source_name: Sam Hopkins, “The CDE property for minuscule lattices”, arXiv:1606.06248 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1606.06248

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of June 2016); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Li–Qu–Li–Fu's permutation trinomial conjecture over finite fields
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, set $q=3^k$, and let ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$ be the finite field with $q^2$ elements. A polynomial is a **permutation trinomial** over ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$ if it has three terms and induces a permutation of ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$. **Li–Qu–Li–Fu's conjecture.** The following assertions hold:

1. If $k$ is even and
 
$$
f(x)=x^{lq+l+5}+x^{(l+5)q+l}-x^{(l-1)q+l+6},
$$

 with $\gcd(5+2l,q-1)=1$, then $f(x)$ is a permutation trinomial over ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$.
2. If
 
$$
f(x)=x^{lq+l+1}-x^{(l+4)q+l-3}+x^{(l-2)q+l+3}
$$

 and $\gcd(1+2l,q-1)=1$, then $f(x)$ is a permutation trinomial over ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$.
3. If
 
$$
f(x)=x^{lq+l+1}+x^{(l+2)q+l-1}-x^{(l-2)q+l+3}
$$

 and $\gcd(1+2l,q-1)=1$, then $f(x)$ is a permutation trinomial over ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$ whenever $k\not\equiv 2\pmod{4}$.

These conjectures concern explicit permutation trinomials over quadratic extensions of fields of characteristic three. The paper proposes them as finite-field permutation problems; no resolution is supplied in the given source context.
record.source_name: Nian Li, “On Two Conjectures about Permutation Trinomials over F_3^2k”, arXiv:1610.04441 (2016).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.04441

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2016).

record.title: Li–Qu–Li–Fu's rational-function permutation conjecture on roots of unity
record.statement:
Let $k$ be a positive integer, set $q=3^k$, and define

$$
\mu_{q+1}=\{x\in{\mathbb F}_{q^2}:x^{q+1}=1\},
$$

the set of $(q+1)$-th roots of unity in ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$. A rational function **permutes** $\mu_{q+1}$ if it is defined on this set and induces a bijection of it. **Li–Qu–Li–Fu's rational-function conjecture.** The following assertions hold:

1. If $k$ is even and
 
$$
g(x)=\frac{-x^7+x^6+x}{x^6+x-1},
$$

 then $g(x)$ permutes $\mu_{q+1}$.
2. If
 
$$
g(x)=\frac{x^6+x^4-1}{-x^7+x^3+x},
$$

 then $g(x)$ permutes $\mu_{q+1}$.
3. If
 
$$
g(x)=\frac{-x^5+x^3+x}{x^4+x^2-1},
$$

 then $g(x)$ permutes $\mu_{q+1}$ whenever $k\not\equiv2\pmod{4}$.

These assertions are presented as an equivalent reformulation of the preceding permutation-trinomial conjecture via the stated criterion for permutation polynomials. The source context gives no resolution of these assertions.
record.source_name: Nian Li, “On Two Conjectures about Permutation Trinomials over F_3^2k”, arXiv:1610.04441 (2016).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.04441

record.title: The simple-polytope lower-interval conjecture for the face lattice of a phase tropical hypersurface
record.statement:
Let $\hat n=\{0,\dots,n\}$, let $\sigma=\langle I_1,\dots,I_k\rangle$ be a cyclic partition of $\hat n$, and let $J\subseteq\hat n$. Write $(\sigma,J)\in\mathcal W$ when $J$ contains elements in at least two of the subsets $I_1,\dots,I_k$; in this case, $\sigma$ divides $J$. The partial order is $(\sigma',J')\preceq(\sigma,J)$ when $\sigma$ is a refinement of $\sigma'$ and $J'\subseteq J$, and define

$$
\mathcal W_{\preceq(\sigma,J)}:=\{(\sigma',J')\in\mathcal W:(\sigma',J')\preceq(\sigma,J)\}.
$$

**Simple-polytope lower-interval conjecture.** For each element $(\sigma,J)\in\mathcal W$, the lower interval $\mathcal W_{\preceq(\sigma,J)}$ is isomorphic to the face lattice of a simple polytope.

This conjecture would describe the local combinatorial structure of the regular CW-complex whose face lattice is $\mathcal W$. The source does not provide evidence of a resolution, so its status remains open.
record.source_name: Gabriel Kerr and Ilia Zharkov, “Phase tropical hypersurfaces”, arXiv:1610.05290 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.05290

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2016).

record.title: Regularity conjecture for intersected polynomial factors
record.statement:
Let $V=\mathbb{F}_2^n$. For any nondecreasing function $r':\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}\to\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$ and parameters $\delta,\eta,r,d$, there exists a constant $K$ such that a polynomial factor $\mathcal{B}$ of $V$, given by the decomposition theorem, has the following property. If $\mathcal{B}$ is defined by polynomials $P_1,\dots,P_C$, define

$$
\Delta_hP_i(x)=P_i(x+h)-P_i(x)-P_i(h)
$$

for $1\leq i\leq C$, and let $S$ be the set of $h\in V$ for which the factor defined by $P_1,\dots,P_C,\Delta_hP_1,\dots,\Delta_hP_C$ is $r'$-regular. **Regularity conjecture.** $S$ contains a subspace of $V$ of codimension at most $K$.

This conjecture is introduced as an additional assumption for a conditional result verifying the critical-threshold conjecture in the case $N=N_{\ell,c,1}$. Its general status is not resolved in the source.
record.source_name: Sammy Luo, “A Counting Lemma for Binary Matroids and Applications to Extremal Problems”, arXiv:1610.09587 (2018).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1610.09587

record.title: Fundamental conjectures on exchange graphs and seeds of cluster algebras
record.statement:
Let $n$ be the rank of a cluster algebra. Its seeds, clusters, cluster variables, mutation equivalence, and exchange graph are understood in the usual sense of cluster algebra theory.

**Exchange graph and seed conjectures.** (a) The exchange graph of a cluster algebra with rank $n$ only depends on the initial exchange matrix; (b) every seed is uniquely determined by its cluster under mutation equivalence; (c) two clusters are adjacent in the exchange graph if and only if they have exactly $n-1$ common cluster variables.

These are fundamental conjectures concerning the combinatorics of cluster algebras. The supplied source describes them as conjectures, while the paper's abstract says that applications of its cluster formula and $D$-matrix pattern solve some fundamental conjectures affirmatively; the supplied material does not identify which of (a)--(c) are resolved.

record.title: Carnevale–Voll's unitary-factor conjecture for Euler–Mahonian distributions
record.statement:
Let $\rho$ be a composition of $N$, and let $R\subseteq [N-1]$ be constructed from $\rho$ as in the source. Write

$$
C_\rho(x,q)=\sum_{w\in S_N^{R^c}}x^{\operatorname{stc}(w)}q^{\ell(w)}.
$$

A **unitary factor** means a nonconstant factor of the form $1+xq^a$.

**Carnevale–Voll's conjecture.** The polynomial $C_\rho(x,q)$ has a unitary factor if and only if $\rho=(\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_m)$ has all parts equal to some odd integer $r$ and $m$ is even. In that case,

$$
C_\rho(x,q)=(1+xq^{\frac{rm}{2}})\widetilde{C}_\rho(x,q),
$$

for some $\widetilde{C}_\rho(x,q)\in\mathbb{Z}[x,q]$ with no unitary factors.

This conjecture characterizes exactly when the bivariate Euler–Mahonian distribution on the relevant symmetric-group quotient has a unitary factor, and specifies that factor and its exponent.
record.source_name: Angela Carnevale, “On some Euler-Mahonian distributions”, arXiv:1612.00426 (2016).

record.title: The sharp stability conjecture for the edge-isoperimetric inequality in the discrete cube
record.statement:
Let $[n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}$, let $\mathcal{P}([n])$ denote the discrete cube, and let $\partial\mathcal{F}$ be the edge boundary of a family $\mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{P}([n])$. Let $\mathcal{L}\subset\mathcal{P}([n])$ be the initial segment of the lexicographic ordering with $|\mathcal{L}|=|\mathcal{F}|$. Two families are **weakly isomorphic** when one can be obtained from the other by a cube automorphism of the relevant type.

**The sharp stability conjecture.** If $\mathcal{F}\subset\mathcal{P}([n])$ and $\mathcal{L}\subset\mathcal{P}([n])$ is as above, then there exists a family $\mathcal{G}\subset\mathcal{P}([n])$ weakly isomorphic to $\mathcal{L}$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{F}\mathbin{\Delta}\mathcal{G}|\leq 2\bigl(|\partial\mathcal{F}|-|\partial\mathcal{L}|\bigr).
$$

The paper proves the same stability statement with an unspecified absolute constant in place of $2$, and explains that the constant $2$ is the conjectured sharp value. The conjecture remains open in the source.
record.source_name: David Ellis, Nathan Keller and Noam Lifshitz, “On the structure of subsets of the discrete cube with small edge boundary”, arXiv:1612.06680 (2018).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.06680

record.title: Constant-energy minimal spectral partitions for symmetric planar domains
record.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a disk, a square, or an equilateral triangle, let $k$ be the number of cells, and let $\mathfrak L_{k,p}(\Omega)$ denote the optimal $p$-norm energy of a $k$-partition. **Symmetric-domain partition conjecture.** The following numerical observations are conjectured: (i) if $\Omega$ is a disk and $k\in\{2,3,4,5\}$, then $\mathfrak L_{k,p}(\Omega)$ is constant with respect to $p$, and an optimal partition consists of $k$ angular sectors of opening $2\pi/k$; (ii) if $\Omega$ is a square and $k\in\{2,4\}$, then $\mathfrak L_{k,p}(\Omega)$ is constant with respect to $p$, with a minimal $2$-partition given by two equal rectangles or two equal right-isosceles triangles, and with the minimal $4$-partition composed of four squares; (iii) if $\Omega$ is an equilateral triangle and $k=n(n+1)/2$ with $n\geq2$, then $\mathfrak L_{k,p}(\Omega)$ is constant with respect to $p$, and a minimal $k$-partition consists of $3$ equal quadrilaterals, $3(n-2)$ pentagons, and $(n-2)(n-3)/2$ regular hexagons. These are numerical observations, and the source relates the third case to the honeycomb conjecture; no proof of the full collection is supplied.
record.source_name: Virginie Bonnaillie-Noel and Beniamin Bogosel, “Minimal Partitions for p-norms of Eigenvalues”, arXiv:1612.07296 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1612.07296

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2016).

record.title: Endpoint behavior of optimal p-norm spectral-partition energies
record.statement:
Let $\Omega$ be a domain, let $k$ be a positive integer, let $\mathfrak L_{k,p}(\Omega)$ be the optimal $p$-norm energy of a $k$-partition, and let $p_{\infty}(\Omega,k)$ denote the parameter introduced in the source. **Endpoint-energy conjecture.** One has

$$
p_{\infty}(\Omega,k)\in\{1,\infty\},
$$

and either $\mathfrak L_{k,p}(\Omega)$ is constant with respect to $p$ or it is strictly increasing with respect to $p$. Moreover, numerical simulations suggest that $p_{\infty}(\Omega,k)=1$ if one of the following holds: $\Omega$ is a disk and $k\in\{2,3,4,5\}$; $\Omega$ is a square and $k\in\{2,4\}$; or $\Omega$ is an equilateral triangle and $k=n(n+1)/2$ with $n\geq1$. The claim summarizes numerical evidence concerning how the optimal energy changes with $p$; it is not presented with a proof, and the source does not provide a general resolution.

record.title: Sparse form domination implies worse sparse form domination
record.statement:
Let $\vec{r}\in(0,\infty)^m$, $q_0\in(0,\infty)$, and $s\in(q_0,\infty]$. Let $T$ be an operator defined on $m$-tuples of functions. Suppose that, for any $f_1,\ldots,f_m\in L^\infty_c(\mathbf{R}^d)$ and some function $g$, there exists a sparse collection $\mathcal{S}$ such that

$$
\|T(\vec{f})\cdot g\|_{L^{q_0}(\mathbf{R}^d)}\lesssim \left(\sum_{Q\in\mathcal{S}}\left(\prod_{j=1}^m\langle f_j\rangle_{r_j,Q}\right)^{q_0}\langle g\rangle^{q_0}_{\frac{1}{\frac{1}{q_0}-\frac{1}{s}},Q}|Q|\right)^{\frac{1}{q_0}}.
$$

**Sparse form domination conjecture.** The same estimate should also hold after replacing $q_0$ by any $q\in(0,q_0]$.

This conjecture asks whether sparse domination in form at exponent $q_0$ automatically yields the corresponding, quantitatively weaker, sparse form estimates at all smaller exponents. The text notes that such replacement would give qualitatively the same weighted bounds, but with a worse exponent; whether the needed flexibility follows automatically is unknown.
record.source_name: Emiel Lorist and Zoe Nieraeth, “Sparse domination implies vector-valued sparse domination”, arXiv:2003.02233 (2021).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2016–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1609.06364](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.06364), [arXiv:1601.03193](https://arxiv.org/abs/1601.03193).

record.title: Sokal's conjecture on functional-digraph component polynomials
record.statement:
Let $\psi_{n,k}$ be the number of functional digraphs on $[n]$ with $k$ weakly connected components, and define

$$
\bm{\psi}_n(y)=\sum_{k=0}^n\psi_{n,k}y^k.
$$

A functional digraph is a directed graph in which every vertex has out-degree $1$; a vertex is cyclic if it lies on a directed cycle. Let $[\psi_{n,k}]_{n,k}$ denote the lower-triangular counting matrix.

**Sokal's functional-digraph conjecture.** The following assertions hold:
(i) $[\psi_{n,k}]_{n,k}$ is totally positive;
(ii) $(\bm{\psi}_n(y))_{n\geq0}$ is coefficientwise Hankel-totally positive in $y$;
(iii) $(\psi_{n+1,1})_{n\geq0}$ is Hankel-totally positive, equivalently, it is a Stieltjes moment sequence.

These assertions concern positivity of functional-digraph enumeration matrices, component polynomials, and the connected case. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Bao-Xuan Zhu, “Coefficientwise Hankel-total positivity of the row-generating polynomials for the output matrices of certain production matrices”, arXiv:2202.03793 (2024).
record.references:

record.title: Hamiltonicity conjecture for one-ended generalized quasi-dihedral groups
record.statement: Let $G=\langle S\rangle$ be a one-ended generalized quasi-dihedral group, and let $\operatorname{Cay}(G,S)$ denote its Cayley graph. A **Hamiltonian double ray** is a spanning double ray, while a **Hamiltonian circle** is a circle in the Freudenthal compactification of the graph that contains all its vertices. **One-ended generalized quasi-dihedral Hamiltonicity conjecture.** The Cayley graph $\operatorname{Cay}(G,S)$ contains a Hamiltonian double ray or a Hamiltonian circle. The paper establishes Hamiltonian double rays and, in the two-ended setting, Hamiltonian circles for the relevant groups; it proposes that the analogous Hamiltonicity statements also hold for one-ended generalized quasi-dihedral groups, where the index-two abelian subgroup is isomorphic to $\mathbb Z^k$ for some $k\geq 2$.
